public_comments.reason: The speaker comments on the perception of the council meetings and the role of a woman of color.
public_comments.text: having thank you thank you good evening again um council members community of the members and my family that's here um lately people have been calling these meetings the janet show and i just heard of that some say with laughs some say with frustration but let's talk about what that really means because if this is the janet show it means a woman of color standing her ground in a place that's really not built for her and let it be the Janet show let her be the star that she is and continues to be if it means growing up speaking up and refusing to be silent in the face of criticism then yes this is the Janet show so let's be clear that phrase is being used to minimize to mock and to dismiss very real work that she has put into this community for the past 10 years and the very real weight of what councilwoman Janet Diaz has carried for this city now on top of that she's being called islamophobic and let me say this plainly that is not who Janet is like I've expressed before she has stood up for immigrants from lower income families for unrepresented voices including Muslims in way that many people in this room never have yes a post was made it landed wrong but she took responsibility she listened and she opened her up she opened herself up to hard conversations this is what growth looks like not perfection but this is what leadership should look like but instead of making space for growth some of us would rather come in here and tear her down why because it is easier to shame than to understand correct because it is easier to label someone than to engage with them and try to get them get to know them better but I'm back here to say, because I was just up here, enough is enough. We cannot let one moment erase a legacy. We cannot let rumors or headlines override someone's truth, the truth that she lived every day and that we've seen that she lives every day. And we absolutely cannot let a woman's courage be turned into a punchline. So if this is a Janet show, then let it be a show of resilience, representation, and real leadership. Janet Diaz deserves our respect, not just us, but the whole community. She deserves our support, and she deserves better than this. Thank you, Janet, for everything you've done for my community, and not just mine, but each and every person that knocks on your door. I've never been able to stay here and text someone and call someone and get an answer right away, and have you come to my house and help me fix each and every problem that my community is facing. There were nights that I could not sleep because someone of my own family has died and deported. I did not know what to do, how to handle that situation. You came through and you helped and you continue to help my community that is full of Hindus, Muslims and Buddhists. So for them to come up here and say that you're Islamic, Islamophobic and all this and that, like I just, I'm so sorry that you have to go through this And thank you for all the support that you continue to give us, no matter the criticism that you face. Thank you, Ms. Kamal.
